title: Tableau Extract Refresh Duration SLA
dataSources: Tableau Server logs (`tableau:backgrounder`, `tableau:vizqlserver`, `tableau:httpd`), `workgroup` repository tables (`background_jobs`, `http_requests`, `_views_stats`, `licensing`) via DB Connect, Tableau Cloud Admin Insights / Activity Log exports.
app: Splunk DB Connect (Splunkbase 2686) against the Tableau Server `workgroup` PostgreSQL repository; Tableau Server logs via Universal Forwarder; Tableau Server REST API and TSM metrics via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=tableau:backgrounder job_type=refresh_extracts finish_code=0
| eval duration_min=round(run_time/60,1)
| stats avg(duration_min) as avg_min, max(duration_min) as max_min, p95(duration_min) as p95_min by job_name
| where p95_min>30
| sort - p95_min
description: Measures how long successful extract refreshes take and flags workbooks whose 95th-percentile refresh time exceeds an SLA, indicating queries or extracts that need optimisation.
value: Long refreshes crowd the Backgrounder queue and push overnight windows into business hours; spotting the slowest extracts lets teams optimise before capacity is exhausted.
implementation: Schedule daily over a trailing 7 days; tune the 30-minute threshold to your Backgrounder window. Pair with the Backgrounder queue-backlog use case for capacity planning.
visualization: Table sorted by p95_min, trend line of refresh duration per workbook.
grandmaExplanation: We measure how long your Tableau reports take to refresh so the slow ones can be sped up before they run late and hold up everything else.
